# Frontend index fixtures

Real data from `Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend`, captured 2026-10-19 for
`test_frontend_index.py`.

- `perf-<ts>-<sha8>.json`: the three newest baselines from the `perf-data`
  branch (`baselines/`), unmodified. The publisher ingests these in the
  end-to-end tests.
- `entries.json`: the compact entries the publisher produces for the twenty
  baselines that were on `perf-data` at capture time (the three raw files
  above plus seventeen older ones, which are not checked in to keep the
  repo small). Generated by ingesting the twenty files oldest first with
  `frontend_index.perf_entry` and classifying each against the entries
  before it, exactly as `write_perf` does.
- `expected_latest_cmp.json`: the comparison of the newest baseline
  (`20261019T130522Z-dd678395`) against the other nineteen, produced by a
  small TypeScript harness run with `npx tsx@4.19.2` that imports
  `computeStats`, `zScore` and `classifyChange` from the frontend's
  `scripts/perf-stats.ts` and copies `meanMetric`, `medianMetric` and
  `computeCV` from `scripts/perf-report.ts`. Two inputs follow the
  publisher rather than the PR report: the history values are the per-run
  means rounded the way the entries store them (8 significant digits, bytes
  to an integer) and `absDelta` is the current median minus the history
  mean (the report compares against the main baseline's median, which a
  main-branch history has no separate copy of). Rows are
  `[current median, history mean, history stddev, history n, z, cls]` per
  metric in `REPORTED_METRICS` order; `history_ids` lists the nineteen
  baselines oldest first.

`test_latest_comparison_matches_the_frontend_report` checks that the
publisher reproduces every row, letter for letter. Regenerate all three
after a change to the metric registry or the rounding rule, from the same
twenty raw files.
